evidence.clarity: Headline 'Dinner is already in your fridge.' is a line rather than a statement of the product; the lede ('plans the week's dinners around it, and the shopping list is only what's missing') makes the product clear. The audience (parents, picky kids) is never named in the first screen at 1440 or 390; it only appears in the dark 'green bits' section about two screens down.
evidence.fit: Uses the supplied waitlist URL on every CTA, says free with price unset ('What it costs'), invents no users or press, and makes the fridge-door demo the memorable hook the brief asked for. The picky-kid audience gets only a text band of four short paragraphs; the demo has no way to express what a kid won't eat, so the brief's main audience tension is described, not shown.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero is product-specific: a dark fridge-door frame with tilted masking-tape ingredient labels that flip to ink when picked, plus a mint taped-on 'Still need to buy' note. Below the hero the page reverts to the stock structure: three numbered yellow-circle steps, a dark band of four text items, a single-paragraph price section, a plain FAQ and a centred CTA band.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the working planner is in the first viewport with its output (Mon/Tue 'Nothing to buy', list with day tags) visible beside the chips. Tapping 'Milk' moved Mac and cheese to Wed and dropped Milk from the list; 'Sausages' brought in 'Breakfast for dinner'. The 'example dinners' label sits only at the bottom of the frame (390: y about 2140, roughly 1,600px below the first chips). Small inconsistency: 'Tuna and sweetcorn pasta bake' needs no sweetcorn.
evidence.craft: Heavy, tightly tracked 800-weight sans headline and the tape chips are well executed. Defects: white on #E8472B CTA text is about 3.9:1 at 18px bold (axe color-contrast, 2 nodes); the fridge 'door handle' (6x64px dark bar at the right edge of the door) reads as a scrollbar at every width; at 1440 the left hero column ends at y=592 leaving about 300px of empty yellow below the CTA; lower sections are a narrow left-aligned column with large dead space to the right at 1440.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow, headline/lede/CTA fit the first screen, no nav so no menu needed. But tape chips are 33-38px tall and 'Shuffle' is a 28px-high text link; the demo starts at y=480 while the dinners begin at y=1235 and the list at y=1920, so tapping a chip at the top of the frame gives no visible feedback without scrolling. Layout is stacked rather than recomposed.
evidence.honesty: No invented proof. But the CTA note says only 'Free to use. iPhone first.'; what joining involves (an email) is said only in the closing band. The example label is late (bottom of the demo). Unsupported specifics in copy: FAQ says 'Android is planned after that', step 1 says 'It takes about a minute the first time', steps claim every dinner is 'thirty minutes or under' and the list is 'sorted by aisle'.
evidence.interaction: Chips are real buttons with aria-pressed, keyboard reachable (Tab: wordmark, header CTA, hero CTA, then Eggs, Cheddar...), Space toggles. Empty state written ('Tap a few things above to start.' / 'The list writes itself once...'); all chips on gives 'Nothing. The whole week is already in the house.' Weak spots: 'Shuffle' mostly reorders the same dinners (1st and 3rd shuffle produced the identical week), there is no reset to the sample, and at 390 results land far below the tap.
evidence.copy: Tight and specific: 'Shop for the gap', 'Made for the table where somebody won't eat the green bits', 'The half bag of spinach gets used on Tuesday instead of thrown away on Sunday', demo rows 'From the house: ... Buy: ...'. 'Shuffle' and 'Questions people ask' are defaults; the hero note is too terse to tell a parent what the waitlist does.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: promise, CTA and a working demo with visible output in one viewport, which is strong. 390: headline, lede and CTA plus the top of the chip grid; no dinner or list is visible, so nothing in view backs the promise. Neither width names the audience.

problems: The picky-kid audience the brief is written for gets no presence in the first screen or the demo; it is only a text band further down.
Mobile demo is a long stack: 33-38px chips, a 28px Shuffle link, and dinners about 750px below the chips, so taps give no visible feedback; the example label is at the very bottom.
Primary CTA text fails contrast (about 3.9:1), and below the hero the page falls back to generic steps/dark band/FAQ/CTA-band sections with dead space at 1440.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Plan the week's dinners from the fridge, not the store.' plus lede 'Pantrywise is a free iPhone app for parents of picky kids. Tick what's in your fridge and cupboard; it plans seven weeknight dinners around that and lists only what's missing.' names what, who and platform; CTA 'Join the iPhone waitlist'. Visible at 1440 and 390 without scrolling.
evidence.fit: Supplied waitlist URL on all CTAs; free now, family plan 'Later' with price unset; no fake proof; the picky-kid tension is resolved in the product itself ('The kids won't eat' chips that adapt the plate, Max 6 / Nora 9 example no-lists). Recipe constraint handled ('not recipes from partners'). Some overbuild: the shopping list appears three times (sheet, mini card, phone mock).
evidence.distinctiveness: A coherent kitchen-fridge system: Bookman-style serif display on yolk, ice-blue shelf panel with drawn ingredient icons, a paper plan sheet held by a tomato magnet, yellow-magnet kid notes, a dashed 'Later' price card. Underneath, the section order (steps, dark band, price cards, FAQ accordion, CTA band, dark footer) is still the familiar template, carried by product-specific mini artifacts.
evidence.proof: Planner starts at y=449 at 1440 with shelf and Mon-Fri visible; labelled 'A sample fridge. Tap what you have.' at the top of the panel and 'Sample shelf, sample dinners...' under the sheet. Ticking 'Nothing mixed in' added KIDS lines to 5 of 7 nights ('egg and peas on the side'); 'Nothing spicy' swapped out Shakshuka. Weaknesses: ticking any of the three unticked items (chickpeas, pasta, yogurt) leaves the plan unchanged except the status count, 'No mushrooms' changes nothing, and the default week needs 7 bought items, which undersells 'only what's missing'. 'Half an onion' is used on three nights.
evidence.craft: Clear type scale (clamped serif H1/H2, Inter body), spacing tokens, consistent 2px ink borders and pill radii; axe reports no violations. Minor: USES/BUY/KIDS tags are 11px uppercase (23 elements), the page is long (5420px at 1440) with repeated egg-fried-rice and list examples, and the 768 layout simply stacks the shelf above the sheet.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow, Menu button opens a 224px panel with 48px links, closes on link tap and on Escape (focus returns to the button). Shelf chips 44-54px, reset 45px. Recomposed in places (2-column shelf, single-column list), but the plan sheet starts at y=1352 and the to-buy list at y=2214, so feedback from a chip tap sits below the fold; total height 8586px.
evidence.honesty: Before the click: 'Free to use. One email address, and we write when the app is ready. A paid family plan with shared lists comes later; its price isn't set.' Sample label at the top of the demo and on every mini example ('Example', 'Example no-list'). Android answered without promising a date. Small unshown claims ('in the order you walk the shop', counted 'in packets and tins') while the demo list isn't aisle-ordered.
evidence.interaction: Checkbox chips with visible focus ring, keyboard reachable after the nav; row flash on changed nights and live status text; empty state ('Nothing on the shelf. Tick at least one thing you have, or this week is just a shopping trip.'), short state ('Only 2 dinners fit...'), 'Put the sample back' resets shelf and vetoes; second list in the phone mock updates too; FAQ details open. Thin spots: three ticks and one veto produce no visible plan change; feedback is off-screen at 390.
evidence.copy: Specific and in the parent's world: 'Picky eaters get a veto, not a lecture', 'It keeps the dinner and changes the plate', 'Big tick targets, because you're holding a basket', 'No card, no trial clock.' Slightly wordy in places, and edge states produce awkward lines ('BUY tin of chickpeas, tortillas and half a bag of spinach', 'buy ... leftover rice').
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific outcome, named audience, CTA with what-happens note, and the live shelf plus five planned nights in view. 390: promise, audience, CTA and note fit, and only the 'On the shelf' panel title and first chips are visible; no output is in view at the phone width.

problems: The demo often doesn't visibly respond: ticking chickpeas, pasta or yogurt, or 'No mushrooms', changes nothing but a counter, and the default week has 7 things to buy.
On the phone the plan and list sit 700-1600px below the chips, and the page is 8586px tall with the same list and dish repeated across sections.
11px uppercase USES/BUY/KIDS tags, and edge-state copy that asks you to 'buy leftover rice' or 'half a bag of spinach'.

reason: B carries the brief's real audience into the artifact itself: the picky-kid veto changes the plate in the demo, the audience is named in the first screen, and the CTA says what joining means before the click, with a type and colour system that holds across sections. A's taped-fridge hero is charming and its demo responds more reliably, but the rest of the page is generic, its CTA fails contrast, and its mobile targets are small. I would switch if B's demo kept producing no visible change for the taps visitors make first, or if its length tested badly on phones.
